title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to the Flood-Affected Vulnerable Population in Girei and Fufore LGAs of Adamawa State.

description.narrative: ltpgtLESGO and CRUDAN are proposing a six-month project in line with the 2025 First Reserve Allocation Strategy, which will provide a timely and effective response to beneficiaries identified through the use of the existing state social register and community validation of the Girei and Fufore LGAs of Adamawa state. It is a known fact that flooding causes an unending calamity that results in food shortages, displacement, and loss of means of livelihoods, as well as destroyed properties and assets. In order to ensure that impacted populations receive timely financial support to fulfil critical needs, this initiative is planned as an anticipatory step to give emergency Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) before the full impact of flooding rises. This will help in the provision of options, dignity, and self-reliance to the affected population in managing their needs in the event of severe flooding.ltbrgtThe intervention will prioritize vulnerable households, including women, children, persons with disabilities, and elderly individuals, who are most at risk of suffering from the effects of flooding. By providing cash transfers before and during the crisis to a targeted 13,092 individuals in selected communities of Damare, Dakri, Gereng and Modire in Girei and Fufore LGA, respectively. Beneficiaries will have the flexibility to purchase essential goods such as food, clean water, medicine, and emergency shelter supplies with the guidance of LESGO in alignment with MEB standard. The project seeks to distribute anticipatory cash assistance to households before flooding intensifies, enabling them to prepare adequately, reduce the need for harmful coping strategies, such as selling assets or skipping meals, enhance food security and health outcomes by ensuring families can afford essential supplies, strengthen resilience by helping households recover faster post-disaster, and support local markets by encouraging beneficiaries to purchase necessities within their communities. The project's implementation plan concentrates on important areas to guarantee that multipurpose financial assistance is delivered efficiently. In order to identify the households most at risk in flood-prone areas, vulnerability assessments and community discussions will be used to carry out targeted beneficiary selection in conjunction with the state social register. Depending on accessibility and security considerations, cash transfer mechanisms will be facilitated through direct bank transfers and/or mobile money services to guarantee that the funds reach recipients safely and effectively. Information campaigns will also be used to raise community awareness and involve the community, educating households on how to best use the monies for recovery and preparedness. A robust monitoring and evaluation system will be built to track the usage of funds and assess the overall impact of the intervention, ensuring transparency and effectiveness.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project will improve coordination for future disaster response planning and readiness by fortifying cooperation between government stakeholders and humanitarian organizations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
